title: JavaScript's event loop, microtasks, macrotasks, and related asynchronous behavior
content:
The event loop manages the execution of synchronous and asynchronous tasks, determining which tasks are executed and in what order. The process involves different types of queues: the call stack, microtask queue, and macro task (or task) queue. The priority of execution depends on the type of task and when it is scheduled.

**1. Call Stack:**
• The call stack executes synchronous code, meaning the current function or code is executed immediately, in the order it's encountered in the program.
• Functions or statements are pushed onto the call stack and executed one by one.
• When the call stack is empty, the event loop checks the other queues.
**2. Microtask Queue (Priority Queue):**
• Microtasks are tasks that are queued through mechanisms like Promises (.then(), .catch(), etc.) or queueMicrotask().
• The microtask queue has higher priority than the macro task queue. After executing all synchronous code in the call stack, the event loop will first check and execute the microtasks before moving to the macro tasks.

**3. Macro Task Queue (Task Queue):**
• Macro tasks are typically tasks scheduled through APIs like setTimeout(), setInterval(), or events (e.g., user input, timers, etc.).
• These tasks have lower priority compared to microtasks.
• After the call stack is empty and all microtasks are processed, the event loop will execute one task from the macro task queue.
